From the top of the hill, 49 meters above sea level, there is a view up and down the coast including and the island Hjelm as well as an inland view over the hilly southern Djursland area, called Mols.
Part of the hill became a protected public area in 1927, and was expanded in 1979 to cover 235 hectares. Today, the hill is within Mols Bjerge National Park, a reserve covering 180 square kilometres.


== Geography ==

According to legend, Jernhatten was formed when a troll named Arn threw a stone at a troll on the island of Hjelm. In retaliation, the troll threw a stone back at Arn which missed its target, but was so large that Arn died of fright. He fell, dead, where he had been when he threw the stone. His body thus formed the ridge along the coast of the area, with his helmet creating Jernhatten. The hill and the nearby island of Hjelm may in fact be named for the resemblance of their domed shapes to war helmets.
